This strategy ensures that I will be considered for my most preferred school first, and only if I am rejected will I be considered for my next most preferred school, and so on. The algorithm protects me by only rejecting me *before* I would have been matched.

My priority at y is 1, but since most applicants favor y, it might be more competitive. My priority at x is 2, and I don't really want to go there anyway.

Therefore, I should stick with my true preferences.

Therefore, I should maintain my preference order: y > x > z > w.
